hypotheses_ranked.cause_if_true: Owned Chromium startup alone creates most of the overload on the four-core host.
hypotheses_ranked.falsifiable_prediction: Before/after process CPU-time brackets spanning the first unsafe interval attribute most incremental CPU time to PID 9449 and descendants; background services contribute little incremental CPU time.
hypotheses_ranked.present_observation: Owned Chromium and helpers were active at the spike, but one ps snapshot cannot measure their share of the interval or explain load 10.58.
hypotheses_ranked.one_variable_discriminator: Record the already supported guarded startup interval process-time bracket across Chromium startup, without changing load thresholds.

hypotheses_ranked.cause_if_true: Independent macOS background services create most of the overload while the owned browser starts.
hypotheses_ranked.falsifiable_prediction: The same process-time bracket assigns most incremental CPU time to non-descendants such as corespeechd/provjobd/SafariLaunchAgen, with comparatively low owned Chromium time.
hypotheses_ranked.present_observation: Those non-descendants were simultaneously active, but the snapshot has no prior rate or duration.
hypotheses_ranked.one_variable_discriminator: Compare owned and non-owned process CPU-time deltas over the same guarded interval.

hypotheses_ranked.cause_if_true: Launching the owned browser triggers macOS services, and the combined startup spike overwhelms the host.
hypotheses_ranked.falsifiable_prediction: Pre-launch non-owned service CPU is low, then rises shortly after Chromium launch alongside owned CPU; a subsequent browser-free guarded observation lacks the service rise.
hypotheses_ranked.present_observation: The service and browser processes coexisted only in one post-launch snapshot; there is no pre-launch service snapshot or process start chronology.
hypotheses_ranked.one_variable_discriminator: Bracket service CPU time immediately before and after browser launch within an authorized, already guarded run.

what_is_proven: The product was untested because the resource guard correctly marked the guest stage invalid after sustained CPU/load pressure. The spike began after artifact preparation and during native Chromium/panel startup; both owned browser descendants and non-owned macOS services were active.
what_is_not_proven: The existing records do not attribute the excess CPU/load to browser code, unrelated host work, or browser-triggered host services. A one-minute load average counts runnable tasks and the one-shot ps %cpu values are not an interval CPU budget. No retry, timeout, threshold, workflow or product-code correction is justified from this evidence.
safe_next_action: Keep all 19 current-source guest Settings cases unverified and continue other admitted product lanes. Before scheduling any further Settings acceptance, capture one pre-launch and one during-launch owned/non-owned process CPU-time bracket inside the existing guarded path, then use normal admission and require a real case report plus normal certificate. Do not dispatch an unmeasured repeat or relocate the job. The current workflow enables MATRX_STARTUP_INTERVAL_DIAGNOSTIC only for guest/member chat, so Settings lacks that bracket today; adding it would be a separately reviewed, costed workflow change.
